references.text: May God Almighty bless you, make you fruitful and give you many descendants
God said to him: 'I am God Almighty. Be fruitful and become many'
When Abram was ninety-nine years old, the Lord appeared to him and said: 'I am God Almighty'
Moses' blessing over Joseph: Blessed by the Lord with the best from heaven, from the dew and from the depths that lie below
'I am your father's God, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob'
May God Almighty (El Shaddai) grant you mercy in the sight of that man
From the Mighty One of Jacob, from him who is the shepherd and rock of Israel
Shares the unique phrase 'fruit of the womb' as a central element in God's blessing on fertility.
Repeats the specific motif of 'fruit from the womb' as a sign of God's abundance, even though the context (restoration) is different.
Intratextual parallel between Isaac's and Jacob's blessings, both concerning dominion over brothers and God's chosen blessing.
